# self-update (npm|go|php) or update (npm|go|php)

Add a per-project dependency updater for the three ecosystems the author works in, either as `self-update <eco>` or as a separate `update <eco>`. The npm sketch:

```bash
$ update npm

function update() {
  local packages=("${@}")
  if [ ${#packages[@]} = 0 ]; then
    IFS=' ' read -r -a packages <<<"$(npm ls --depth=0 --prod --json |
      jq -r '.dependencies | keys | join(" ")')"
  fi
  for pkg in "${packages[@]}"; do
    npm install "${pkg}"@latest
  done
}
```

i.e. enumerate the project's direct dependencies (or take them as arguments) and move each to `@latest`; the same for Go modules and Composer packages.

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/278#issuecomment-5711694659
Code vs intent: the three `which` lookups at the top of `bin/update` run under `set -e`; a host missing any one of go/npm/composer cannot use the script at all. `composer` is declared in no host Brewfile (see #140), so on a host provisioned purely from the Brewfiles `update` is unusable.
